title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 322
paragraphs: As this Egyptian Sesostris was returning and bringing back with him many men of the nations whose lands he had subdued, when he came (said the priests) to Daphnae in the district of Pelusium on his journey home, his brother — to whom Sesostris had entrusted the charge of Egypt — invited him, and with him his sons, to a feast; and then he piled up brushwood round the house and set it on fire. Sesostris, when he discovered this, immediately took counsel with his wife (for he was bringing his wife also with him, they said), and she counselled him to lay out upon the pyre two of his sons (of whom he had six), and so make a bridge over the burning mass, that they passing over their bodies should thus escape. This, they said, Sesostris did, and two of his sons were burnt to death in this way, but the rest got away safely with their father.
